title: SOFA (organ failure score)

inputs.label: Respiration: PaO2/FiO2 ratio and respiratory support status
Cardiovascular: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) or vasopressor requirement (doses in ug/kg/min administered for at least 1 hour)
Central Nervous System: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)

bands.text: No organ dysfunction on the six components.
Higher score = more organ dysfunction. A component score of 3-4 means organ failure; an acute rise of 2 or more from baseline with suspected infection meets the Sepsis-3 definition.

source: Vincent JL, Moreno R, Takala J, Willatts S, De Mendonça A, Bruining H, Reinhart CK, Suter PM, Thijs LG. The SOFA (Sepsis-related Organ Failure Assessment) score to describe organ dysfunction/failure. Intensive Care Med. 1996 Jul;22(7):707-710. doi:10.1007/BF01709751
limits: Use the worst value in each 24 hours. Vasoactive doses are micrograms/kg/min for at least 1 hour. Sedation makes GCS hard to judge. The 1996 paper gave no total-score mortality bands.

title: qSOFA (quick sepsis screen)
specialty: Emergency Medicine / Critical Care / Internal Medicine

inputs.label: Altered mentation (Glasgow Coma Scale < 15 in derivation model; <= 13 in Sepsis-3 consensus table)

bands.text: Below the higher-risk threshold. This does not exclude sepsis.
Higher risk of poor outcome in suspected infection. Look for organ dysfunction (full SOFA) and escalate.

source: Seymour CW, Liu VX, Iwashyna TJ, Brunkhorst FM, Rea TD, Scherag A, Rubenfeld G, Kahn JM, Shankar-Hari M, Singer M, Deutschman CS, Escobar GJ, Angus DC. Assessment of Clinical Criteria for Sepsis: For the Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA. 2016 Feb 23;315(8):762-774. doi:10.1001/jama.2016.0288
limits: A prognostic prompt, not a diagnosis and not a rule-out test. Altered mentation is scored here as GCS below 15 (the Sepsis-3 bedside version); the derivation paper used GCS 13 or less.

title: HEART score (chest pain)

inputs.label: History (clinical suspicion based on chest pain pattern, onset, radiation, and relief with nitrates)

options.label: Moderately suspicious (both specific and non-specific elements)
Nonspecific repolarisation disturbance (or LBBB, pacemaker, LVH, digoxin effect, no significant ST depression)
Significant ST-segment depression or elevation in absence of bundle branch block, LVH, or digoxin

inputs.label: Risk factors (diabetes mellitus, current/recent smoker, hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, family history of CAD, obesity) or atherosclerotic history (MI, PCI/CABG, stroke/TIA, peripheral arterial disease)

options.label: >= 3 risk factors or history of atherosclerotic disease

inputs.label: Troponin on admission, as a multiple of the assay threshold
inputs.unit: multiple of upper limit of normal (ULN)

bands.text: Lower risk (2.5% major cardiac events in the original cohort).
Intermediate risk (20.3% in the original cohort). Usually observation, serial troponin and further testing.
Higher risk (72.7% in the original cohort). Usually early cardiology involvement.

source: Six AJ, Backus BE, Kelder JC. Chest pain in the emergency room: value of the HEART score. Neth Heart J. 2008 Jun;16(6):191-196. doi:10.1007/BF03086144
limits: Original 2008 version: troponin cut-offs are 1x and 2x the assay threshold (later work used 3x). Age 65 or more scores 2. Cohort rates are not universal probabilities. Always use serial troponin and the local pathway.

title: TIMI risk score (UA/NSTEMI)

inputs.label: >= 3 risk factors for coronary artery disease (family history of CAD, hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, diabetes, or current smoker)
ST-segment deviation (>= 0.5 mm depression or transient elevation) on ECG at presentation
Use of aspirin in prior 7 days
Elevated serum cardiac markers (CK-MB or cardiac-specific troponin level)

source: Antman EM, Cohen M, Bernink PJLM, McCabe CH, Horacek T, Papuchis G, Mautner B, Corbalan R, Radley D, Braunwald E. The TIMI Risk Score for Unstable Angina/Non-ST Elevation MI: A Method for Prognostication and Therapeutic Decision Making. JAMA. 2000 Aug 16;284(7):835-842. doi:10.1001/jama.284.7.835
limits: For UA/NSTEMI, not the separate TIMI STEMI score or undifferentiated chest-pain exclusion. The original endpoint combined all-cause death, new or recurrent myocardial infarction, and severe recurrent ischemia requiring urgent revascularization through 14 days. Percentages are original test-cohort observations, not isolated mortality risks.

title: NIHSS (stroke severity)

options.label: Not alert; but arousable by minor stimulation
Not alert; requires repeated stimulation to attend
Responds only with reflex motor or autonomic effects or totally unresponsive
Answers one question correctly (or endotracheal tube/dysarthria/trauma barrier)

inputs.label: 1c. LOC Commands (open/close eyes, grip/release non-paretic hand)

options.label: Forced deviation, or total gaze paresis not overcome by oculocephalic maneuver
Minor paralysis (flattened nasolabial fold, asymmetry on smiling)
Partial paralysis (total or near-total paralysis of lower face)
Complete paralysis of one or both sides (absence of facial movement in upper and lower face)

inputs.label: 5a. Motor Arm - Left (hold at 90 degrees sitting or 45 degrees supine for 10 seconds)

options.label: No drift for full 10 seconds (or amputation/joint fusion = untestable, 0)
Drift before full 10 seconds; does not hit bed
Some effort against gravity; cannot sustain position, drifts to bed
No effort against gravity; limb falls

inputs.label: 5b. Motor Arm - Right (hold at 90 degrees sitting or 45 degrees supine for 10 seconds)

options.label: No drift for full 10 seconds (or amputation/joint fusion = untestable, 0)
Drift before full 10 seconds; does not hit bed
Some effort against gravity; cannot sustain position, drifts to bed
No effort against gravity; limb falls

inputs.label: 6a. Motor Leg - Left (hold at 30 degrees supine for 5 seconds)

options.label: No drift for full 5 seconds (or amputation/joint fusion = untestable, 0)
Drift by the end of 5 seconds; does not hit bed
Some effort against gravity; limb falls to bed within 5 seconds
No effort against gravity; leg falls to bed immediately

inputs.label: 6b. Motor Leg - Right (hold at 30 degrees supine for 5 seconds)

options.label: No drift for full 5 seconds (or amputation/joint fusion = untestable, 0)
Drift by the end of 5 seconds; does not hit bed
Some effort against gravity; limb falls to bed within 5 seconds
No effort against gravity; leg falls to bed immediately
Severe to total sensory loss (or coma/quadriplegic/bilateral loss)
Mute, global aphasia; no usable speech or auditory comprehension (or coma)
Visual, tactile, auditory, spatial, or personal inattention to bilateral simultaneous stimulation in 1 modality
Profound hemi-inattention or extinction to more than one modality

bands.text: No measured deficit. Stroke is not excluded.

source: Brott T, Adams HP Jr, Olinger CP, Marler JR, Barsan WG, Biller J, Spilker J, Holleran R, Eberle R, Hertzberg V. Measurements of acute cerebral infarction: a clinical examination scale. Stroke. 1989 Jul;20(7):864-870. doi:10.1161/01.str.20.7.864
limits: Severity bands are the commonly used groupings, not from the 1989 paper. Use the official NINDS instructions and stimuli. Items that cannot be tested (amputation, joint fusion, intubation for speech) are scored per the official manual and not guessed. Under-detects posterior circulation strokes.

title: ABCD2 (stroke risk after TIA)

inputs.label: Blood pressure >= 140 mmHg systolic OR >= 90 mmHg diastolic at first evaluation after TIA

bands.text: Low risk: 2-day stroke risk 1.0%, 7-day risk 1.2%, 90-day risk 3.1%.
Moderate risk: 2-day stroke risk 4.1%, 7-day risk 5.9%, 90-day risk 9.8%.
High risk: 2-day stroke risk 8.1%, 7-day risk 11.7%, 90-day risk 17.8%.

source: Johnston SC, Rothwell PM, Nguyen-Huynh MN, Giles MF, Elkins JS, Bernstein AL, Sidney S. Validation and refinement of scores to predict very early stroke risk after transient ischaemic attack. Lancet. 2007 Jan 27;369(9558):283-292. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(07)60150-0
limits: clinicalFeatures examples contain selected points; age and duration are raw values. Clinical-feature points are mutually exclusive. Developed after a clinical diagnosis of TIA; it does not establish that diagnosis. Low scores do not exclude an urgent vascular cause. Original cohort risks are not universal contemporary probabilities.

title: Alvarado score (appendicitis)

inputs.label: Migration of pain to the right lower quadrant (RLQ)
Tenderness in the right lower quadrant
Elevation of temperature (>= 37.3 C / 99.1 F oral)
Shift to the left of neutrophils (> 75% neutrophils)

bands.text: Below the score described as compatible with appendicitis; appendicitis is not excluded.

source: Alvarado A. A practical score for the early diagnosis of acute appendicitis. Ann Emerg Med. 1986 May;15(5):557-564. doi:10.1016/S0196-0644(86)80993-3
limits: Maximum 10. Temperature threshold 37.3 C or more; white cell count above 10,000/uL; left shift taken as neutrophils above 75%. The exact original boundaries are reported differently in different sources. Less reliable in women of childbearing age, children and the elderly.

title: Child-Pugh (cirrhosis class)

inputs.label: Serum bilirubin (Note: for primary biliary cirrhosis, cut-offs in Pugh 1973 are < 4, 4-10, and > 10 mg/dL)
Prothrombin time (seconds prolonged above control in original 1973 table; or modern INR equivalent)

source: Pugh RNH, Murray-Lyon IM, Dawson JL, Pietroni MC, Williams R. Transection of the oesophagus for bleeding oesophageal varices. Br J Surg. 1973 Aug;60(8):646-649. doi:10.1002/bjs.1800600817
limits: Use prothrombin time OR INR, never both. Grading of ascites and encephalopathy is partly subjective. Cholestatic bilirubin variants are not included.

title: MELD (liver disease severity)

inputs.label: Dialysis 2 or more times in the last 7 days

bands.text: Low risk: 1.9% estimated 3-month mortality in hospitalized patients.
Critical risk (capped at 40 for UNOS allocation): 71.3% estimated 3-month mortality.

source: Kamath PS, Wiesner RH, Malinchoc M, Kremers W, Therneau TM, Kosberg CL, D'Amico G, Dickson ER, Kim WR. A model to predict survival in patients with end-stage liver disease. Hepatology. 2001 Feb;33(2):464-470. doi:10.1053/jhep.2001.22172
limits: Uses the classic UNOS equation: 3.78 ln(bilirubin) + 11.2 ln(INR) + 9.57 ln(creatinine) + 6.43, with lower bound 1.0 for each value, creatinine capped at 4.0 (set to 4.0 if dialysis twice in 7 days). Score is limited to 6-40. Not a transplant allocation tool; MELD-Na and MELD 3.0 differ.

title: PHQ-9 (depression)

inputs.label: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Feeling down, depressed, or hopeless
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Feeling tired or having little energy
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Poor appetite or overeating
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Feeling bad about yourself — or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed? Or the opposite — being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

source: Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JBW. The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. Journal of General Internal Medicine. 2001;16:606-613. doi:10.1046/j.1525-1497.2001.016009606.x
limits: Examples contain selected response points. The additional functional-difficulty question is not included in the 0-27 total. Severity bands are not a standalone diagnosis. The PHQ diagnostic algorithm is distinct from simple total-score classification. Any positive item 9 requires a separate safety assessment regardless of the total; item 9 alone is not a complete suicide-risk assessment. Do not silently score missing answers as zero.

alerts.text: Item 9 is positive. Do a direct suicide-risk assessment now and follow your local safety pathway, whatever the total.

title: GAD-7 (anxiety)

inputs.label: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Not being able to stop or control worrying
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Worrying too much about different things
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Trouble relaxing
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Being so restless that it is hard to sit still
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Becoming easily annoyed or irritable
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

inputs.label: Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen
inputs.unit: frequency during the past two weeks

source: Spitzer RL, Kroenke K, Williams JBW, Lowe B. A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: the GAD-7. Archives of Internal Medicine. 2006;166:1092-1097. doi:10.1001/archinte.166.10.1092
limits: Examples contain selected response points. The supplementary functional-difficulty question is not part of the 0-21 total. The original screening threshold >=10 had sensitivity 89% and specificity 82% in the validation sample. A two-week symptom score does not establish the diagnostic duration or exclusions required for generalized anxiety disorder. Do not silently score missing answers as zero.

title: Apgar score (newborn)

options.label: Active movement with good flexion and resistance to extension
Slow or irregular; weak respiratory effort
Good breathing with a strong cry

bands.text: Low five-minute score in term and late-preterm infants; later AAP/ACOG interpretation.
Moderately abnormal five-minute score in term and late-preterm infants; later AAP/ACOG interpretation.
Reassuring five-minute score in term and late-preterm infants; later AAP/ACOG interpretation.

source: Apgar V. A proposal for a new method of evaluation of the newborn infant. Current Researches in Anesthesia and Analgesia. 1953;32:260-267. doi:10.1213/00000539-195301000-00041
limits: Choice examples contain selected points; pulse is a raw heart rate. Original assessment was at 60 seconds after complete birth. Later practice records separate scores at one and five minutes; do not add scores across time. The bands supplied are later AAP/ACOG five-minute interpretations, not bands attributed to the 1953 paper. Original prose includes heart rate 100 in the two-point category; some published tables instead print >100. The score does not determine whether initial resuscitation is needed, diagnose asphyxia by itself, or predict an individual infant's neurological outcome.

title: PERC rule (low-risk PE)

inputs.label: Surgery or trauma within 4 weeks requiring hospitalization

bands.text: PERC negative only if eligible low-pretest-probability patient
PERC positive: rule cannot exclude PE

source: Kline JA, Mitchell AM, Kabrhel C, Richman PB, Courtney DM. Clinical criteria to prevent unnecessary diagnostic testing in emergency department patients with suspected pulmonary embolism. J Thromb Haemost. 2004;2:1247-1255. doi:10.1111/j.1538-7836.2004.00790.x
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. PERC is an eight-criterion exclusion rule, not a validated graded probability score. Numerical total is an implementation count only. Apply only after clinician assessment establishes low PE pretest probability, conventionally <15%. Do not use in high probability, instability, or as a validated pregnancy rule. Oxygen saturation assumes whole-percentage recording; the original publication expresses the negative threshold as >94%. Do not round a borderline decimal measurement silently.

title: HAS-BLED (bleeding risk on anticoagulation)

inputs.label: Dialysis, renal transplant, or creatinine >=200 micromol/L
Chronic liver disease OR bilirubin >2x ULN with AST/ALT/ALP >3x ULN
Previous bleeding or predisposition, such as anemia
Unstable/high INRs or poor time in therapeutic range, e.g. <60%

bands.text: Below high-risk threshold; correct modifiable bleeding risks
High bleeding risk; caution and closer review

source: Pisters R, Lane DA, Nieuwlaat R, de Vos CB, Crijns HJGM, Lip GYH. A novel user-friendly score (HAS-BLED) to assess 1-year risk of major bleeding in patients with atrial fibrillation: the Euro Heart Survey. Chest. 2010;138:1093-1100. doi:10.1378/chest.10-0134
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. Renal/liver dysfunction and drugs/alcohol each contribute independently, maximum 9. Labile INR concerns VKA therapy; absent INR data cannot establish stable anticoagulation. High score alone must not be used to withhold anticoagulation. Absolute risks at very high scores are imprecise; no invented annual percentages. Alcohol units follow source definition; a unit is not interchangeable with every national standard drink.

title: Glasgow-Blatchford (upper GI bleed)

inputs.label: Hemoglobin category, using published male/female thresholds

options.label: Male >=12.0 and <13.0 g/dL OR female >=10.0 and <12.0 g/dL

bands.text: Original very-low-risk category; assess clinical suitability

source: Blatchford O, Murray WR, Blatchford M. A risk score to predict need for treatment for upper-gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Lancet. 2000;356:1318-1321. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(00)02816-6
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. Pre-endoscopic adult upper-GI bleeding score. Urea mmol/L differs from BUN mg/dL. Sex-specific hemoglobin categories must be selected correctly. Bands deliberately represent the original score-zero threshold; no universal mild/moderate/severe bands exist. Some subsequent guidelines accept 0-1 for selected outpatient management; the score alone never authorizes discharge. Maximum 23.

title: Centor score (sore throat)
source: Centor RM, Witherspoon JM, Dalton HP, Brody CE, Link K. The diagnosis of strep throat in adults in the emergency room. Med Decis Making. 1981;1:239-246. doi:10.1177/0272989X8100100304
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. Original adult emergency-department derivation; no age adjustment. Original fever variable is history of fever, not an invented measured-temperature cutoff. Culture probabilities are cohort estimates, not universal calibration. Does not confirm GAS or exclude airway/deep-neck emergencies. Follow current testing and antimicrobial guidance.

title: McIsaac score (sore throat)

bands.text: Original pathway: no culture or antibiotic
Original pathway: no culture or antibiotic
Original pathway: throat culture; treat if positive
Original pathway allowed empirical treatment or culture; use current guidance

source: McIsaac WJ, White D, Tannenbaum D, Low DE. A clinical score to reduce unnecessary antibiotic use in patients with sore throat. CMAJ. 1998;158:75-83. PMID 9475915.
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. For ages >=3 years. Temperature threshold follows the 1998 table (>38 C); later descriptions sometimes use >=38 C, so do not mix versions. DOI not verified; PMID supplied. Historical management bands are not a current antibiotic recommendation; testing policies differ by age, setting and rheumatic-fever risk. The maximum attainable score for age >=45 years is 3.

title: Ranson criteria (pancreatitis, non-gallstone)

inputs.label: During first 48 hours: hematocrit fall >10 percentage points
During first 48 hours: BUN rise >5 mg/dL despite IV hydration
During first 48 hours: serum calcium <8 mg/dL
During first 48 hours: arterial PaO2 <60 mmHg
During first 48 hours: base deficit >4 mEq/L
During first 48 hours: estimated fluid sequestration >6 L

source: Ranson JH, Rifkind KM, Roses DF, Fink SD, Eng K, Spencer FC. Prognostic signs and the role of operative management in acute pancreatitis. Surg Gynecol Obstet. 1974;139:69-81. PMID 4834279.
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. Full assessment requires admission and 48-hour data; do not treat an admission subtotal as the final score. Do not mix biliary and original thresholds. Numeric comparisons follow the cited primary comparison table: strictly greater than for hematocrit fall and BUN rise. Hematocrit fall means percentage-point change, not relative percent. BUN is not serum urea. Estimated sequestration is not simply IV fluid administered. Historical prognostic classification is not the Revised Atlanta severity definition; organ failure and clinical deterioration require immediate assessment. Original DOI not verified; PMID supplied. No unverified mortality percentages assigned.

title: Ranson criteria (pancreatitis, gallstone)

inputs.label: During first 48 hours: hematocrit fall >10 percentage points
During first 48 hours: BUN rise >2 mg/dL despite IV hydration
During first 48 hours: serum calcium <8 mg/dL
During first 48 hours: base deficit >5 mEq/L
During first 48 hours: estimated fluid sequestration >4 L

source: Ranson JH. Etiological and prognostic factors in human acute pancreatitis: a review. Am J Gastroenterol. 1982;77:633-638. PMID 7051819.
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. Full assessment requires admission and 48-hour data; do not treat an admission subtotal as the final score. Do not mix biliary and original thresholds. Numeric comparisons follow the cited primary comparison table: strictly greater than for hematocrit fall and BUN rise. Hematocrit fall means percentage-point change, not relative percent. BUN is not serum urea. Estimated sequestration is not simply IV fluid administered. Historical prognostic classification is not the Revised Atlanta severity definition; organ failure and clinical deterioration require immediate assessment. Original DOI not verified; PMID supplied. No unverified mortality percentages assigned.

title: Padua score (VTE prophylaxis)

inputs.label: Active cancer: metastases and/or chemotherapy/radiotherapy within 6 months
Previous VTE, excluding superficial vein thrombosis
Anticipated bed rest with bathroom privileges for >=3 days
Known thrombophilia, including antithrombin/protein C/S deficiency, FVL, prothrombin mutation or APS

bands.text: Low VTE risk by original model
High VTE risk by original model

source: Barbar S, Noventa F, Rossetto V, et al. A risk assessment model for the identification of hospitalized medical patients at risk for venous thromboembolism: the Padua Prediction Score. J Thromb Haemost. 2010;8:2450-2457. doi:10.1111/j.1538-7836.2010.04044.x
limits: All inputs are required. Missing, unknown, invalid, or inapplicable data must not be scored as zero. Bands use inclusive endpoints and cover attainable totals only. Educational definition; clinical judgment and current local pathways remain necessary. Adult medical inpatients; predicts VTE risk for prophylaxis assessment, not diagnosis of symptomatic VTE. Combined OR items count once, not once per component. Assess bleeding risk and contraindications separately before prophylaxis. Retains original >=4 high-risk threshold; local modified thresholds are different implementations. Maximum 20.

title: Bishop score (cervix, original)

inputs.label: Fetal station using the original station convention

bands.text: Below the original favorable threshold; this range is not a universal indication for cervical ripening.
Favorable by the original >8 threshold; assess all obstetric indications and contraindications separately.

source: Bishop EH. Pelvic scoring for elective induction. Obstet Gynecol. 1964;24:266–268. Original table reproduced by CMQCC:
limits: Choice inputs and examples contain selected component points, not option indexes or raw measurements. Integer total 0–13. Do not substitute modified Bishop tables. The original table uses discrete examination categories; mapping intermediate measurements, dilation outside 0–6 cm, or station outside the listed categories is UNSURE and must not be interpolated automatically. Favorability thresholds differ between later protocols. This score does not establish that induction is safe.

title: Ottawa ankle and foot rules

inputs.label: Bone tenderness at posterior edge or tip of lateral malleolus, distal 6 cm
Bone tenderness at posterior edge or tip of medial malleolus, distal 6 cm
Bone tenderness at the base of the fifth metatarsal
Unable to bear weight for four steps immediately after injury
Unable to bear weight for four steps at clinical assessment

bands.text: Neither regional rule indicates radiography, provided the patient is eligible.
Radiography indicated for each region whose regional expression is true.

source: Stiell IG et al. Decision rules for the use of radiography in acute ankle injuries: refinement and prospective validation. JAMA. 1993;269:1127–1132. Operational criteria: British Columbia, Ankle Injury guideline, 2014. doi:10.1001/jama.269.9.1127
limits: This is a decision rule, not an additive score. Expected values 0 and 1 encode negative and positive results only; no clinical point weights are invented. Evaluate ankle and foot expressions separately to select imaging; both may be positive. Limping still counts as weight-bearing if four independent steps are possible. The weight-bearing criterion requires inability at BOTH times. This implementation follows the cited adult guideline scope, age ≥19; it excludes pregnancy, multiple painful injuries, cognitive impairment and lower-limb sensory deficits. Pediatric use requires a separately validated scope. Negative results do not exclude every injury. Reassess persistent pain or impaired weight-bearing after 5–7 days. Missing or unreliable findings must block calculation rather than default to false.

title: Canadian CT head rule

inputs.label: GCS <15 at two hours after injury
Suspected open or depressed skull fracture
Any sign of basal skull fracture
Pedestrian struck, vehicle occupant ejected, or fall >3 feet or five stairs

bands.text: Rule negative in an eligible patient; clinical assessment and appropriate observation remain necessary.

source: Stiell IG et al. The Canadian CT Head Rule for patients with minor head injury. Lancet. 2001;357:1391–1396. Original rule reproduced in Stiell et al., JAMA 2005;294:1511–1518: doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(00)04561-X
limits: Boolean decision rule, not a point total; 0/1 are output encodings. First five inputs are high-risk factors for neurological intervention; last two are medium-risk factors for clinically important brain injury. Eligibility must be checked before evaluation: age ≥16, acute blunt head injury within 24 hours, initial GCS 13–15, and witnessed loss of consciousness, definite amnesia or witnessed disorientation. Do not apply to minimal injury without these features, anticoagulation or bleeding disorders, post-traumatic seizure, acute focal neurological deficit, penetrating injury, or an otherwise excluded patient. These patients need independent assessment. Basal fracture signs include hemotympanum, periorbital bruising, Battle sign and CSF leakage. Original rule reproductions differ from some later adaptations at the amnesia/fall boundaries; this definition uses >30 minutes and >3 feet or five stairs, without silently substituting ≥30 minutes or ≥1 metre. Missing findings must block calculation.

title: CIWA-Ar (alcohol withdrawal)

bands.text: Severe reference range, ASAM 2020; evaluate complications independently.

source: Sullivan JT et al. Assessment of alcohol withdrawal: the revised Clinical Institute Withdrawal Assessment for Alcohol scale (CIWA-Ar). Br J Addict. 1989;84:1353–1357. Freely reproducible instrument: doi:10.1111/j.1360-0443.1989.tb00737.x
limits: Selected points are input values. Integer total 0–67. Unanchored means the original instrument supplies that number without a separate verbal descriptor; none is invented here. Labels are abbreviated: trained assessors must consult the complete instrument. Heart rate and blood pressure are not summed. ASAM bands are later clinical reference ranges, not original diagnostic boundaries. Do not diagnose withdrawal or prescribe treatment from the total alone. Communication barriers, sedation, delirium and concurrent illness can invalidate ratings; use an appropriate alternative assessment. Seizures or delirium require urgent management regardless of total. Unknown items must block calculation.

title: CAGE (alcohol screen)

inputs.label: Ever felt you should reduce your drinking?
Ever been annoyed by criticism of your drinking?
Ever felt guilty or bad about your drinking?
Ever used a morning drink to settle nerves or relieve a hangover?

bands.text: Below the usual ≥2 positive threshold; does not exclude harmful alcohol use.
Positive screen; assess alcohol use and related problems further.

source: Ewing JA. Detecting alcoholism: the CAGE questionnaire. JAMA. 1984;252:1905–1907. Public-domain status documented by Flinders University NCETA: doi:10.1001/jama.1984.03350140051025
limits: Selected points are input values. Integer total 0–4. Original lifetime alcohol screen; do not silently change to current drinking or other substances. Screening is not a diagnosis and is less suited to detecting hazardous consumption without dependence. Any concerning answer warrants discussion even below the usual threshold. Labels are concise paraphrases; use the validated wording and translation for formal administration. Missing answers must not be scored as No.

title: Modified Rankin Scale

options.label: Symptoms without significant disability; usual activities preserved
Slight disability; previous activities restricted, own affairs managed independently
Moderate disability; needs some help, walks without another person's assistance
Moderately severe disability; needs help walking and attending bodily needs
Severe disability; bedridden, incontinent, constant care required

source: van Swieten JC et al. Interobserver agreement for the assessment of handicap in stroke patients. Stroke. 1988;19:604–607. Operational categories: doi:10.1161/01.STR.19.5.604
limits: Single ordinal category, not an additive checklist. Input is the selected category's points. Record assessment time and distinguish pre-stroke from follow-up disability. Use a trained assessor and standardized interview when appropriate. Joint Commission administrative codes 7 and 8 are not mRS clinical scores and are excluded. Unknown status is missing, never death or zero.

title: Rockall score (after endoscopy)

options.label: Heart failure, ischemic heart disease or other major comorbidity
Renal failure, liver failure or disseminated malignancy
Mallory–Weiss tear, or no lesion with no bleeding stigmata
Other diagnosis excluding upper gastrointestinal malignancy
Upper GI blood, adherent clot, visible or spurting vessel

bands.text: Higher scores mean higher risk of death and rebleeding. There is no single universal low/high cut-off; use your local pathway.

source: Rockall TA et al. Risk assessment after acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage. Gut. 1996;38:316–321. doi:10.1136/gut.38.3.316
limits: Selected component points are inputs; integer total 0–11. This record requires endoscopic diagnosis and stigmata. Pre-endoscopy Rockall uses only age + shock + comorbidity, range 0–7, and requires a separate definition and interpretation. Choose one highest applicable comorbidity category; do not sum diseases. SBP <100 takes precedence regardless of pulse. Do not assign zero to unperformed endoscopy or unknown findings. Some secondary tables contain boundary transcription errors; age 80 belongs in the ≥80 category, and SBP exactly 100 belongs in an SBP ≥100 category. The total does not replace resuscitation or establish discharge eligibility.

title: Pediatric Appendicitis Score

inputs.label: Pain migration to right lower quadrant
Right lower quadrant tenderness with cough, percussion or hopping

bands.text: Low-risk group in the cited Johns Hopkins pathway; not an independent exclusion of appendicitis.
Indeterminate group in the cited Johns Hopkins pathway.
High-risk group in the cited Johns Hopkins pathway; assess urgently, not an automatic operative diagnosis.

source: Samuel M. Pediatric appendicitis score. J Pediatr Surg. 2002;37:877–881. doi:10.1053/jpsu.2002.32893
limits: Selected points are input values. Integer total 0–10. Fever is taken as 38.0 C or above (Johns Hopkins pathway version). Risk bands are explicitly from the later Hopkins pathway, not claimed as original Samuel bands. Original study population was children aged 4–15. Do not replace ANC with neutrophil percentage or combine this score with Alvarado weights. Missing laboratory or examination findings must not default to zero. Clinical deterioration, peritonism or persistent concern overrides a low score.
